_help: Web issues of the BotsDoThat Weekly. Each issue lists 3-5 use-case slugs (outcome, prompt and sources are pulled from data/use-cases.json at build time), one new or improved page, an optional watch-out (news id from data/news.json) and a sponsor (null = house ad). Optional: preview (email preview text) and watch_out_label (heading for the watch-out, default "One thing that went wrong"). sent_on stays null until the issue is emailed to subscribers. Optional (issue 6+): today_line (one sentence pointing to /today/), changes (list of {id: news id, note: one plain line}; label via changes_label), jobs_of_day (list of {date, slug, note} from that week's Today editions; label via jobs_label) and items_label (heading above the numbered items). Old issues without them render as before.

issues.subject: 4 jobs you can hand to an AI this week
issues.intro: Welcome to the first BotsDoThat Weekly. Each week we pick a few real, practical jobs people are handing to AI, tell you what you end up with, and give you a prompt you can copy. No hype, no made-up numbers.

items.why: Shopping for a car? Paste the listing link before you book a viewing, and walk in with the right questions.
If a fall fix-up is on your list, let an agent draft the messages to local trades and collect their replies in one table. You approve every message first.
For the long videos and threads you keep meaning to get to: one reply saves a short summary for later.
If any of your bots run on autopilot, put a hard cap on what they can spend.

new_page.note: Write a fact sheet once, let a browser agent type it into the employer's careers page, sign in yourself, and stop before Submit. It also covers what to keep out of the chat and the job-scam signs the FTC warns about.

issues.subject: Let AI shop, plan and sort for you (it asks first)
issues.preview: Four jobs to hand to AI this week, each with a prompt to copy, plus how to keep an agent away from files you care about.
issues.intro: This week's picks are about AI that does things, not just answers: buying, booking, sorting and nudging. Each prompt below tells the AI to stop and ask you before any money moves or anything gets shared or deleted. Copy one, fill in the brackets, and try it.

items.why: Holiday lists are starting. Shopify's free Shop connection lets ChatGPT or Claude search stores and check out with Shop Pay, and you approve every purchase. Your card number never goes to the AI.

Friendsgiving or a weekend away stuck in a 60-message thread? Instinct's group-chat agent opened to all iMessage users on Oct 27. It collects dates and budgets, suggests options and books only when someone says so.
After Halloween and fall trips, ask Gemini to pull the best shots into a private album. The prompt tells it to leave your originals alone. It's rolling out gradually, so you may not have it yet.
If your calendar runs your week, have an assistant watch it and text you only when something needs a decision, with one fix ready and quiet hours you choose.

new_page.note: Before an agent works on your computer, give it one folder of copies, keep a backup it can't reach, and turn on its sandbox or ask-first setting. The guide has setup notes for Claude Cowork, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes, plus the real cases where agents wiped files.

issues.subject: Hand AI your shopping list, your raise talk and your day plan
issues.preview: Four everyday jobs to hand to AI this week, each with a prompt to copy, plus how to keep your chats out of AI training.
issues.intro: This week's picks are small, everyday jobs: filling a grocery cart, rehearsing a pay conversation, planning your day and decoding a tax letter. Each prompt keeps you in charge, so the AI suggests and you decide. Copy one, fill in the brackets, and try it.

items.why: Snap your handwritten grocery list and Walmart's Sparky agent matches each item to your usual store and past buys. You check the cart and pay. It's for U.S. shoppers in the Walmart app and on walmart.com.
Review season is coming for a lot of people. Let AI help you pick a number from real pay data, draft a friendly counteroffer, then play your manager so you can rehearse first.
Say "plan my day" and an assistant connected to your calendar and task list proposes a time-blocked plan with breaks. Nothing goes on your calendar until you approve it.
Got a confusing tax letter or form? AI is good at explaining what a box means and listing questions for your preparer. Tests show it gets the math wrong, so don't let it fill in or file anything.

new_page.note: Paying for ChatGPT or Gemini doesn't automatically keep your chats out of model training. The guide shows where to switch it off in each app, how to re-check it later, and a new note: share links stay visible to anyone who has the link even with training off, so strip personal details before you share.

issues.subject: Let AI book your flight and take errands from your car or watch
issues.preview: Four jobs to hand to AI this week, each with a prompt to copy, plus a new guide to writing instructions your agent actually follows.
issues.intro: This week's picks are about handing jobs to AI when your hands are busy: booking a holiday flight, passing along errands from the car or your wrist, and letting agents search public data on a question you care about. Each prompt tells the AI to stop and ask you before anything is booked, paid or sent. Copy one, fill in the brackets, and try it.

items.why: Booking holiday travel? An agent can compare fares and fill in passenger details, then stop for your OK before paying. New this week: United now blocks personal AI agents from booking, so on some airlines you'll let the agent find the fare and finish checkout yourself.

Since Nov 11, Gemini works on Apple CarPlay, so ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Gemini can all be reached from the car screen. Talk through your to-dos on the drive, and the prompt makes it hold anything that sends or buys until you've parked and checked.

Meta's Muse agent now has an Apple Watch and Wear OS app. Ask for movie tickets or a calendar fix from your wrist and approve the result when it's ready. Save bigger payments for your phone, where you can read the details.

A weekend project: two hobbyists pointed AI agents at free NASA data. One found what turned out to be an already-mapped Maya site; the other turned up two signals now listed as planet candidates. The prompt asks the agents to try to prove each lead wrong.

new_page.title: How to write instructions for an AI agent
new_page.note: Good agent instructions say six things in plain sentences: the one job, what it may read, the steps, what the result looks like, what it must ask you first, and what to do when it's unsure. The new guide has a template to copy, 3 filled-in examples, where to paste them in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and a 3-minute test.

issues.subject: A scam-check bot for your parent, plus 3 AI jobs
issues.preview: Four jobs to hand to AI this week, each with a prompt to copy, plus a step-by-step guide to Gemini's newly free Tasks.
issues.intro: This week's picks are about AI that looks out for you: a scam checker your mom or dad can text before sending money, an assistant that phones the car shops so you don't sit on hold, a morning brief for your meetings and a training check-in from your watch. Each prompt tells the AI to stop and ask you before anything is booked, sent or paid. Copy one, fill in the brackets, and try it.

items.why: Set up one bot with clear scam-checking instructions and share it with an older parent. When a scary call, text or email arrives ("your grandson is in jail"), they text the bot first and get a calm answer and one safe next step, like calling the relative back on a saved number. It's a second opinion, not a guarantee, so the prompt sends every money request back to a call with you.

Tasks in Gemini became free on Nov 17, and in the US it can phone businesses for you (Grok Bot and paid Muse plans can too). The prompt has it call nearby shops, find a slot that fits your calendar and check with you before booking. It won't agree to repairs, prices or deposits on the call.

Save this once as a daily task in Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude or Grok Bot. Each weekday morning you get one short page: what each meeting is about, the emails behind it, what you promised to bring and the replies you owe. It can draft replies, but it never sends, accepts or moves anything without your yes.

Connect your Garmin (or Oura, Strava or Withings) data to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok and get a short morning note on your sleep, HRV and recent training, with one suggested session for today. It shows you any workout before putting it on your watch. It's coaching guidance, not medical advice.

new_page.title: How to use Tasks in Gemini (now free)
new_page.note: Tasks in Gemini (it used to be called Gemini Spark) has been free since Nov 17 with a personal Google account in the US, Canada, India, Japan, South Korea and Australia. The new guide covers the Chat-to-Task toggle, 7 setup steps with a read-only first task to copy, what free gets you versus Google AI Pro or Ultra, and 6 safety rules.

issues.subject: Secret Santa, gift lists and a ChatGPT limits change
issues.preview: This week's biggest AI changes in plain words, the four jobs of the day, and four more problems to hand to AI, each with a prompt to copy.
issues.intro: Happy Thanksgiving. This week's Today editions leaned toward the holidays: a dinner plan, a gift list that tracks order-by dates, store calls to check what's in stock and a package check. Below are the week's biggest changes in plain words, those four jobs of the day, and four more problems you can hand to AI, each with a prompt to copy. Every prompt spells out what the AI must not do without your OK.
issues.today_line: BotsDoThat Today is a short daily edition (about 3 minutes): the 3 changes in AI assistants that day, what each means for you, and one job to try.

changes.note: If you pay for ChatGPT and use GPT-6.2 Astra or Sol, the same work now uses more of your allowance (OpenAI says limits come 40% sooner on Astra and 25% on Sol after it fixed a launch undercount). Every Go, Plus, Pro and Business account gets one banked reset: redeem it in Usage settings on the web or desktop app once an allowance is below 80%.

From December, chats, agent work and Codex coding on Plus, Pro and Business draw from one allowance. Quick chats with the Instant model stay unlimited; check the combined total in Settings, then Usage.
Paid ChatGPT plans get GPT-6.2 Sol in the normal Chat tab over the coming days, with nothing to turn on. Free and Go plans aren't part of this update.

In the US you can now fill a Target, Albertsons, Safeway or Shaw's grocery order inside Google Search or the Gemini app. You link each account yourself, so connect only the stores you want Google to use.

On iPhone, share your camera in Gemini Live and it describes what it sees and tells you how to aim, for things like a nutrition label or a washing-machine dial. Google says it can make mistakes and isn't a mobility aid.

jobs_of_day.note: One list of every package and where it really is, plus a drafted note to the store for any that went wrong.
A short table of which nearby stores have it today, so you make one trip instead of five calls.
The menu, who brings what, an oven timeline that works back from dinner time and a shopping list.
Ideas for everyone on your list, a running total and a weekly 'still to buy' note before shipping cut-offs.

issues.items_label: Four more problems to hand to AI this week

items.why: Your bot does the busywork of a family or office Secret Santa: the kick-off email, passing each wish list to the right gift-giver and nudging late ones. A proper draw tool picks the names, not the chatbot, so nobody (you included) sees the matches. You approve every email, and it's worth asking the bot what's still waiting for your OK so nobody gets missed.

If you're home for the holiday and your mom or dad struggles with small keyboards, set up a free assistant they can talk to (ChatGPT Voice, Gemini Live or Meta Muse) on their own phone. Practise with their real to-do list together. The prompt keeps them in charge: nothing is sent, paid or signed until they say yes out loud.

Keep the booking you have, then have your bot watch for cancellations at the doctor, tire shop or barber and move you up when a time you can make opens. You choose whether it asks first or books straight away. It never cancels the old booking until the new one is confirmed, and it never pays a deposit.

If your bot reads your email or browses for you, a stranger can hide instructions in a message or web page. No company says this is solved. Paste this standing rule into your bot's instructions so anything it reads is treated as information, not orders, and it comes back to you before it sends, shares or spends anything.

new_page.title: How to use ChatGPT dots: who gets it, setup, first job
new_page.note: ChatGPT dots, OpenAI's personal agents, are on Pro, rolling out to selected Plus users, and on Business and eligible Enterprise workspaces (18+, not in the EU, EEA, UK or Switzerland, and not on the free plan). The new guide has a who-gets-it table, 7 setup steps with a read-only first job to copy, the 4 Custom rules choices, good first jobs and 6 rules to set before it acts.

issues.watch_out_label: One thing to keep in mind
